naming: The loader reads the document with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Always mapping: this document fills one OSDU template.
The mapping's name. With version it makes the reference Name@version a delivery flow pins under render.mapping, and the file is mappings/Name@version.yaml.
The mapping's version. It is part of the reference Name@version and of every rendered record's render context, so a new version re-renders the records that use it.
Free text describing what the mapping delivers.
The saved template version the mapping fills. A run refuses to render against any other, and one the catalog does not hold stops the run.
The OSDU kind of the records the mapping renders, authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch, such as osdu:wks:work-product-component--WellLog:1.4.0.
The saved template version: the 16 hexadecimal characters the Templates page and 'sqlflow template list' show for the kind.
The rows the mapping renders: the source system, the key the delivery key and the OSDU id are derived from, and what identifies a record to a person.
The source system. It enters the delivery key, and so the OSDU id: two mappings that deliver the same rows into the same entity type and partition need different systems or keys.

The columns of the dataset's own row that identify a record, in order, each named as it is (log_id). The delivery key, and so the OSDU id, is derived from them; a key column need not be written into the record.
A key column, named as it is, such as log_id.

Optional display text for the ledger and the GUI, with {<column>} tokens naming columns of the dataset's own row, such as "{wellbore_uwi} / {log_id}", cut at 400 characters. It never enters the record.

Optional columns of the dataset's own row whose values identify the record to a person (a wellbore id, a log id), each named as it is. The ledger indexes every value, so the Records page finds the record by any of them. Search only: never in the record.
An identifying column, named as it is, such as wellbore_uwi.
Values the flow supplies under render.parameters, each declared here. dataPartition is always declared, and a flow value for a parameter the mapping does not declare is refused.
One parameter, read in a literal's text and in an id template as {$param.<name>}.
True when the flow has to supply the parameter (or it has a default).
The value used when the flow supplies none. It is mapping content and is not expanded as a reference.
Free text describing the parameter.
The record sets the mapping's $search nodes look in on the platform, as each record needs one, rather than capturing them into the cache. One search per kind, each read by a node.
One search, read by a node as $search: <name>.
The kind searched: one entity type, at one version or every version, such as osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:*.
The saved template whose schema says how the searched kind's properties are indexed, so a $findBy line is asked the way the platform answers it.
The kind of the saved template, such as osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:1.3.0.
The saved template version: 16 hexadecimal characters.
Free text describing the search.

The records a row is matched to once in the cache and read wherever the record needs them, such as the log's wellbore, whose id the record writes and whose field and country key its access groups. Every node reading a lookup reads the record it finds, so two values derived from one record never come from two. Each lookup is read by a node.

One lookup, read as $lookup: <name>.<field> or in a $findAll line as $lookup.<name>.<field>: $cache: <Type> names the cached type, $findBy (one line or a list of <field> = <column> or <field> = 'text', read against the dataset's own row and tried in order) finds the record, with $modifiers on the value compared, $ignoreSeparators and $description beside them.

The record the mapping renders, laid out the way the rendered record is: acl, legal, tags and data, and the properties below them. Every word of the mapping language starts with '$' ($from, $forEach...); every other key is a property of the record, so no template's property name is ever read as the language. A property that is not written is left out of the record.

A property of the record, written as one of four nodes. A literal is the value it is: text, a number, a boolean or a list, such as ReferenceCurveID: MD. Its text reads a parameter as {$param.<name>} and no other token. An object is a map of the property names it holds, each a node in turn. A value node is a map whose keys all start with '$'. It reads one value with $from: <column>, $expr: <expression>, $value: <literal>, $cache: <Type>.<field>, $search: <name> or $lookup: <lookup>.<field> (a field of the record a lookup of the lookups block finds, taking only $when, $required and $description beside it), and takes beside it $findBy (with $cache and $search: one line or a list of <field> = <column> or <field> = 'text', tried in order), $findAll (with $cache, in place of $findBy: every row of the type that meets one line <field> = <column>, <field> = 'text' or <field> = $lookup.<lookup>.<field>, each of whose values is a key, and any number of lines <field> is empty; the node gives the field it reads from every such row as a list, a value two rows give written once), $modifiers (a list applied top to bottom: trim, upper, lower, split: { separator, part }, replace: { <value>: <value or ~> } with otherwise beside it, or replace: $cache.<Type> with match, field and otherwise beside it, equals: <text>, date or date: <format>, number or number: { decimal, group }, id: "<template>", or ref, ref: <Entity> or ref: <group>--<Entity>, the reference {$param.dataPartition}:<group>--<Entity>:{$value}: to the record whose code is the value, of the type the property points to; id or ref is always the last), $when (a condition: an expression giving true or false, such as log_status = "FINAL" or not empty(curve_unit); false leaves the property out), $required (true by default: an empty value holds the record; false leaves the property out), $ignoreSeparators (with $cache), $unverified (true on a node that builds an id with id or ref: the id is written even when the cache holds records of its entity type and not this one, recorded as an unverified reference) and $description. A $coalesce node takes the first of several alternatives that gives a value: $coalesce: a list of two or more nodes, each reading one value with $from, $expr, $value, $cache or $search and its own $findBy, $modifiers, $ignoreSeparators and $unverified, tried in order; an alternative that gives nothing passes to the next, a literal $value can only be the last, and $when, $required and $description are written beside the list, since they decide for all of them. A $forEach node repeats the rows of a child dataset as the items of an array: $forEach: <child dataset>, and $item laying out the properties each row fills, with $where (a condition each child row must hold to become an item), $when (decides for the whole array), $required and $description. A list some of whose items are value nodes is a list of values: each item is a literal or a value node (never $coalesce or $forEach), and the list is what they give in order, a value given twice (whatever its case) written once; acl.owners and acl.viewers take one with at least one literal, and the legal lists never do. A list some of whose items are objects is a list of objects: each item is an object laid out as the record tree, whose properties are literals, objects, value nodes, $coalesce nodes or lists of values (never $forEach, and never a list of objects of its own) reading the row the list is in, or an object written as the literal it is; the list is the objects its items give in order, an object given twice written once, and an item none of whose properties gives a value adds nothing. A bare column name reads the row the node is in: the dataset's own row, or under $forEach the item's row; $dataset.<column> reads the dataset's own row from anywhere. An id template reads {$value}, {<column>}, {$dataset.<column>}, {$cache.<Type>.<field>} and {$param.<name>}. A property whose own name starts with '$' is written with one more, $$<name>; what $value holds is written verbatim. An expression reads a column by its name (in backticks when the name is a keyword, starts with a digit or holds '-'), $dataset.<column> and $param.<name>, and writes text in quotes; it compares with =, !=, <, <=, >, >= and in [ ... ], joins conditions with and, or and not, joins text with &, computes with + - * /, and calls iif(condition, value, other), coalesce(value, value, ...), nullif(value, other), empty(value), trim(text), upper(text), lower(text), substring(text, start, length), left(text, count), right(text, count), replace(text, find, with), length(text), contains(text, part), startsWith(text, part), endsWith(text, part), number(value), text(value), round(number, digits) and abs(number). Text compares ignoring case and surrounding spaces; no value is the same only as no value; arithmetic on no value gives no value.

The access control list every OSDU record carries: owners and viewers, each a literal list of at least one entitlements group, such as owners: ["{$param.aclOwner}"]. A DSPDM business object row has none.

The legal block every OSDU record carries: legaltags and otherRelevantDataCountries, each a literal list of at least one value, free of repeats, such as legaltags: ["{$param.legalTag}"] and otherRelevantDataCountries: [NO]. A DSPDM business object row has none.
Free keys of the record, each a text: a literal, such as DeliveredBy: osdu-delivery, or a value node, such as SourceProject: { $from: source_project }.

The record's data, laid out as the template names its properties: each a literal, an object of properties, a value node ($from, $expr, $value, $cache or $search with its settings, or $coalesce listing several of them to take the first that gives a value) a $forEach array whose $item lays out what each row of a child dataset fills, or a list of values or of objects some of whose items read values.
